children: Air India Group gained market share as IndiGo’s share declined, with Akasa retaining its position during August

The domestic air passenger traffic declined 6.34 per cent year-on-year to 121.26 lakh in August 2026, compared with 129.47 lakh passengers carried by Indian airlines in August 2025, according to Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) data released on Wednesday.

The decline in August weighed on the overall passenger numbers for the year, with domestic airlines carrying 1,105.30 lakh passengers during January-August 2026. This was marginally lower than the 1,107.26 lakh passengers recorded during the corresponding period of the previous year, marking an annual decline of 0.18 per cent.

IndiGo continued to have the largest share of the domestic aviation market in August, although its share fell to 65 per cent from 67.4 per cent in July. The airline therefore recorded a sequential decline of 2.4 percentage points in its market share during the month.

Air India Group, meanwhile, increased its market share to 26.7 per cent in August, gaining 2.7 percentage points from July. SpiceJet’s share declined to 1.2 per cent from 1.6 per cent, while Akasa Air retained its 5.5 per cent share during the month.

IndiGo recorded the highest on-time performance (OTP) among scheduled domestic airlines at the 10 major airports in August, with 91.5 per cent of its flights operating on time. Akasa Air followed with an OTP of 90.5 per cent during the month.

Air India Group recorded an OTP of 83.9 per cent at the 10 major airports in August, according to DGCA data. The overall cancellation rate among scheduled domestic airlines stood at 1.39 per cent during the month.
